C12 and C24 provide looser structural analogues for letters acknowledging and praising submitted reports, but their wording and subject matter are less specifically connected.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Thank you for transmitting to me the report on the New England economy submitted to the Council of Economic Advisers.","parent_excerpt":"Last spring the Council of Economic Advisers appointed a Committee of Experts on the New England Economy to prepare an analysis of New England economic opportunities and problems, which is now nearing completion.","explanation":"The parent identifies the precise New England economic study whose completed report is acknowledged in the child."},{"child_excerpt":"Studies of regional economic problems can be a valuable aid in development of national economic policies","parent_excerpt":"the economic growth and stability of an area depends largely upon how its natural resources are developed","explanation":"Both frame analysis of a region's economic conditions as relevant to broader governmental planning."},{"child_excerpt":"this study of New England's long-run problems will contribute to future planning for the economic growth and progress of the nation","parent_excerpt":"providing the blueprints for the most effective development of the resources of this important area of our country","explanation":"The child reuses the parent's future-oriented planning rationale, adapting it from resource development to general economic growth."}]}
